entries.note: PMID 21976485 (PNAS, epub 2011-10-05). Quote verbatim in abstract (truncated mid-sentence). Opening untested at 2009 matches NCT00865904 start; HBE is the system the class relied on.

PMID 21825083, epub 2011-08-08, print 2012. Quote verbatim. NCT00865904 results 2015-08-28 (estimated). Sweat moved, nasal PD and rectal maturation did not: same + partial is right. Pairing, correctly comparison_stated false.

SEC 6-K exh 99.1 quote verbatim; PK 'did not impact the exposure', so not a PK miss. de Wilde 2019 (PMC6521598) full text shows 'further increase in Cl current' with the same triple in HBE. Add-on design attributes the null to GLPG2737.
EC50 81 nM verbatim. No source compares the cell EC50 with human free exposure; untested opening is correct.
PharmR 206038 l.826-832: rat NOAEL '3- or 7-fold', dog 2-fold, verbatim. Wainwright quote verbatim (PMID 25981758). Margin is published only in the 2015 NDA review, after Phase 3; see rule question.
Same Van Goor abstract; 'a level associated with mild CF' is the stated prediction of benefit. Untested opening fine.

Primary FEV1 met (2.6-4.0 points, P<0.001); NCT01807923 results 2015-08-31. FDA PharmR l.1244-1246 is a tier-2 stated comparison calling translation 'limited'; source_calls_it could be over_predicted. Mono FEV1 decline was never a primary endpoint.
PharmR l.435 verbatim; rat plethysmography clean at 250-1000 mg/kg (l.1909). Not scoring respiratory events is defensible. Lumacaftor liver-related SAEs (label 5.2) not discussed; see missing.

Quote and IntegratedR margin verified. But the fatal liver cases are on Trikafta, not vanzacaftor; the label attributes liver injury to the combination products, not to a class drug (#70). Alyftrek's own LFT rises lack a placebo arm.
entries.adjudication_note: Decision 12 (#70): the label attributes fatal liver injury to Trikafta, a combination without vanzacaftor, not to a class drug. Decision 16: a predicted organ with misplaced margin belongs in dose, never safety contra.

entries.note: Dekkers 2013 abstract quote verbatim (PMID 23727931). Organoid assay first run 2013, after Clancy 2012 (epub 2011) and Vertex's 2012 Phase 2 sweat-chloride data: retro, class level is right. VX-809 use from full text not re-seen.

Berkers 2019 abstract quote verbatim (PMID 30759382). Full text 403 again. Abstract says the assay 'can prospectively select' and some rare-mutation patients got off-label drug on organoid response, so retrodiction likely false; lumacaftor/ivacaftor share and within-arm correlation still unverified.
Quote verbatim in bundled 210491 SumR (Study 107 selection rule). FRT was used to select Study 107 patients with no comparison yet; untested 2015 holds.

Castellani 2026 abstract quote verbatim (PMID 41738096). 445-124 enrolled only FRT-responsive non-F508del variants, so prospective; sweat chloride -28.3 is the engagement readout. Same, patient level, 2024 (registry) holds.

Dekkers 2013 abstract quote verbatim. Organoids made no stated efficacy prediction; untested 2013 is an acceptable placeholder, but see efficacy 4: lumacaftor/ivacaftor FEV1 benefit was already public in 2012.

Wainwright 2015 quote verbatim. But Vertex's May/June 2012 Phase 2 releases already reported FEV1 +8.5 points vs placebo in F508del homozygotes on VX-809+ivacaftor, before Dekkers 2013. Class-level answer was known when organoids were first run: retro, not same.
entries.adjudication_note: Decisions 10 and 4: the 2012 Phase 2 (Boyle 2014, PMID 24973281) missed its sweat-chloride primary in cohorts 2/3; FEV1 +5.6 was secondary, so no efficacy patient result preceded Dekkers 2013, which the trial did not motivate.

entries.note: Dekkers 2016 STM abstract quote verbatim (PMID 27334259): correlation with 'published outcome data' is a retrodiction; retro, patient level holds. Pooled with ivacaftor genotype groups, as noted.

Berkers 2019 quote verbatim but abstract only. FEV1 changes are observational on-label/off-label responses, not a trial primary endpoint, and the lumacaftor/ivacaftor subset correlation is unverified; if it does not hold alone, drop the entry.
Same SumR selection-rule quote, verbatim. Untested 2015 for the FRT track with a tezacaftor combination holds.
Quote verbatim in 210491 SumR. FDA checked 'consistency of in vitro assay findings with clinical efficacy data' for the modified TEZ/IVA assay submitted after EVOLVE/EXPAND: retro, class level holds.

Quote verbatim, but it is the same NDA-time consistency check as efficacy 8: the modified TEZ/IVA assay was run for the NDA after Studies 106/107/108 read out. Study 107's FRT rule defined minimal function, not a TEZ/IVA failure prediction. Retro, not same.
entries.adjudication_note: Decision 10: SumR describes an NDA-time 'consistency' check of the modified TEZ/IVA FRT assay against Studies 106/107/108 already read out; Study 107's FRT rule defined minimal function, not predicted failure. Duplicates efficacy 8.

entries.note: Quote verbatim in 212273s002 label (fetched). The ≥10% call 'predictive or reasonably expected to predict' rests on trials already read out; no patient outcome for the 177 added variants existed in 2020. Regulatory reliance, scored retro.
entries.adjudication_note: Decisions 10 and 14: the label's FRT-vs-clinical-response statement rests on trials already read out; the 177 added variants had no patient outcome until 445-124 (efficacy 11). Regulatory reliance is a flag, not a status.

entries.note: Castellani 2026 abstract quote verbatim; primary ppFEV1 +9.2 in FRT-selected variants. Prospective, so same, patient level, 2024. With efficacy 9 and 10 retro, this is the FRT track's first prospective same (decision 10).

entries.rule: untested means a model existed and nobody compared it
entries.note: Pranke 2017 Sci Rep (nature.com full text, published 2017-08-07) abstract quote verbatim. Lumacaftor/tezacaftor rescue in HNE with no prospective patient comparison; untested 2017 opening for the cf-hne-isc track holds.

entries.rule: A model built or run after the clinic already knew the answer is a retrodiction: retro, never same
entries.note: Quote verbatim. Nasal cells sampled pre-treatment, but correlation (R2=0.95, n=8) was drawn after 6-month FEV1 was known and after Orkambi's FEV1 benefit was public (2014-15); no stated pre-outcome prediction. retrodiction: true, as Dekkers 2016 (efficacy 5).
entries.adjudication_note: Retrodiction rule (run after the answer was known): Pranke methods say nasal cells were 'always sampled before starting' Orkambi; cultures read weeks later, before 6-month FEV1. Patient-level answer unknown then; same, low confidence, n=7 members.

entries.rule: stated same-drug comparison, primary endpoint met, model run before the trial
entries.note: Davies 2018 NEJM (PMID 30334693, epub 2018-10-18) conclusion quote verbatim in abstract; ppFEV1 is a primary endpoint (P<0.001). Bamocaftor HBE selection preceded NCT03224351/NCT03029455, so prospective. Inconsistent with efficacy 2's note excluding Keating 2018 as a repeat.

missing: Elexacaftor tox (NDA 212273 MultidisciplineR p.43): rat target organs stomach/testes, no liver; dog only hepatocellular hypertrophy (non-adverse). Trikafta 2019 label 5.1 'Elevated transaminases have been observed in patients with CF treated with TRIKAFTA', later liver failure. Candidate safety entry for model elexacaftor-rat-dog-tox, subject to the same #70 attribution question as safety 2.

Lumacaftor liver: Orkambi 2015 label 5.2/6.1, 'Three patients who received ORKAMBI had liver-related serious adverse reactions ... compared to none in the placebo group', rats and dogs silent on liver (PharmR l.435). Weak because transaminase rates were similar to placebo; the draft should at least note it in safety 1.

Galicaftor HBE model side exists (Wang 2018 J Med Chem, doi 10.1021/acs.jmedchem.7b01339) for the NCT04853368 FEV1 miss (cohort 2 vs placebo 0.9, p=0.402, verified on CT.gov). The draft says no model prediction was found; the judgement should cite this paper and say why it is not scored (combination with non-member correctors).

PELICAN (NCT03474042, GLPG2737 on Orkambi, sweat chloride primary met, no posted results) is a same-drug match on the same HBE model; it belongs in the engagement judgement (it is mentioned) but could be its own dated tier-5 entry before the 2019 contra.

Patient nasal epithelial cell cultures (HNE): Pranke 2017 Sci Rep, doi 10.1038/s41598-017-07504-1 (PMID 28785019), 'Correction of CFTR function in nasal epithelial cells ... predicts improvement of respiratory function by CFTR modulators' (lumacaftor/ivacaftor); later Thorax 2026 doi 10.1136/thorax-2025-223153 on sequential modulators. No parallel track in the draft.

Keating 2018 NEJM (doi 10.1056/NEJMoa1807120, elexacaftor VX-445 HBE + Phase 2, NCT03227471) states the same HBE-to-FEV1 translation as Davies 2018; if efficacy 14 (bamocaftor) is kept as its own f508del-hbe-ussing entry, elexacaftor's stated comparison should be one too, or efficacy 2's note excluding it should cover both.
rule_questions: Decision 16 / checker brief: does a tox margin first published in the NDA review (after Phase 3) count as 'stated before the trial' when the studies themselves were in the IND before Phase 3 (model_filed true)?

Decision 16 says a harm the model predicted with a misplaced margin is counted in dose, but its dose contra row is for a target never reached. Where does a predicted-organ, misplaced-margin harm go when patients reached target and the harm was not dose-limiting (vanzacaftor liver)? Safety contra, safety same, or dose contra?

#70 for fixed-dose combinations whose components are all class members or the shared backbone (Trikafta, Alyftrek): can a label harm attributed to the combination anchor a contra for the corrector's tox model?

Same drug, two combinations, opposite engagement results on the same model (GLPG2737: FALCON null, PELICAN positive). Decision 6 says one drug's contra beats another drug's same; it does not say how one drug's mixed record is resolved.
